# crywolf

Bayesian false-positive occupancy models for data from automated
detectors, with simulation-based checks of whether the correction is
calibrated for your design.

Acoustic classifiers and other automated detectors return false
positives. **crywolf** fits the multiple-methods (site-confirmation)
false-positive occupancy model of Miller et al. (2011) in Stan: the
classifier output may be wrong, and a verified subset of detections is
certain. It also fits the observation-confirmation design of Chambert et
al. (2015), in which an expert checks the observations of some automated
occasions. The false-positive rate can be constant or depend on site
covariates, which matters when false positives track the same
environmental gradient as the species.

## Installation

crywolf is distributed through
[R-universe](https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev), which provides binaries
for Windows, macOS and Linux. The command below also installs ‘cmdstanr’
from the Stan R-universe; CmdStan itself is installed once with
`install_cmdstan()`:

``` r

install.packages("crywolf", repos = c("https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev",
                                      "https://stan-dev.r-universe.dev",
                                      getOption("repos")))
cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()
```

crywolf needs CmdStan 2.40 or later (since crywolf 1.7.0). If you
installed CmdStan before September 2026, update it with
[`cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()`](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/reference/install_cmdstan.html);
[`cmdstanr::cmdstan_version()`](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/reference/set_cmdstan_path.html)
shows the version in use.

The development version can be installed from GitHub with
`remotes::install_github("diogoprov/crywolf")`.

## Example

``` r

library(crywolf)

# simulated data in which false positives track a gradient correlated
# with the occupancy covariate
sim <- simulate_fp(nsite = 300, nocc = 20, conf_effect = 1.5,
                   conf_cor = 0.7, seed = 2026)

# the simulated recorders have no effect, so leave the recorder term out
m0 <- fp_occu(sim$data, occ = ~ x, fp = ~ 1, random_recorder = FALSE)  # constant rate
m1 <- fp_occu(sim$data, occ = ~ x, fp = ~ x, random_recorder = FALSE)  # rate depends on x

coef(m0, "occ"); coef(m1, "occ")                # true slope: -0.8
loo::loo_compare(loo(m0), loo(m1))

# is a constant rate calibrated for this design, and does verifying more help?
fp_verification_curve(nsite = 300, nocc = 20, conf_effect = 1.5,
                      conf_cor = 0.7,
                      models = list(constant = ~ 1, fp_on_x = ~ x),
                      reps = 50)
```

## Main functions

| Function | Purpose |
|----|----|
| [`fp_read_birdnet()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_read_birdnet.md), [`fp_read_validation()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_read_validation.md), [`fp_aggregate()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_aggregate.md) | read BirdNET selection tables and reviewed clips, and build the automated occasions |
| [`fp_threshold_sweep()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_threshold_sweep.md) | fit the model at several classifier thresholds |
| [`fp_data()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_data.md), [`fp_data_wide()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_data_wide.md) | assemble automated, verified, and confirmed detections and site covariates |
| [`fp_occu()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_occu.md) | fit the model; methods `print`, `summary`, `coef`, `predict`, `loo`, `as_draws_df` |
| [`fp_priors()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_priors.md), [`fp_gap_prior()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_gap_prior.md), [`fp_prior_predictive()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_prior_predictive.md) | prior settings, a prior from validated detections, and what the priors imply for data like yours |
| [`fp_ppc()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_ppc.md) | posterior predictive check of the detections per site |
| [`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html), [`fp_effects()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_effects.md), [`fp_sites()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_sites.md) | coefficients and diagnostics, marginal effects, and the probability that each site is occupied |
| [`simulate_fp()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/simulate_fp.md) | simulate data under homogeneous, unstructured, or structured false positives |
| [`fp_calibrate()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_calibrate.md) | coverage and bias of the credible intervals for a design, by simulation |
| [`fp_verification_curve()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_verification_curve.md) | coverage against the fraction of sites verified |
| [`fp_calibrate_fit()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_calibrate_fit.md), [`fp_sbc()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_sbc.md) | calibration on data simulated from a fit, and simulation-based calibration of the computation |
| [`loo()`](https://mc-stan.org/loo/reference/loo.html), [`fp_loo_weights()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_loo_weights.md) | leave-one-site-out cross-validation (exact refits for unreliable sites) and stacking weights |
| [`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) | coverage or bias of a calibration run |
| `curiango` | acoustic monitoring of the Common Pauraque in the Pantanal (Piatti et al. 2026) |

## Related tools

- [fpcalib](https://github.com/diogoprov/fpcalib) is the research
  compendium of the simulation study behind the calibration checks
  (<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23379100>). `simulate_fp(seed = s)`
  reproduces its datasets exactly.
- [sheepdog](https://github.com/diogoprov/sheepdog)
  (<https://provetelab.org/sheepdog/>,
  <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22696210>) is an R package that cuts
  audio clips from BirdNET predictions for manual review and records the
  verdict on each clip, which can feed the verified or confirmed data of
  [`fp_data()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_data.md). It
  is distributed through the same R-universe as crywolf:
  `install.packages("sheepdog", repos = c("https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos")))`.
  From version 2.0.0 it writes `clip_manifest.csv` and
  `validation_by_clip.csv` with English column names;
  [`fp_read_validation()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_read_validation.md)
  reads these and the files of earlier versions
  (`validacao_por_clipe.csv`). The models in crywolf treat the checked
  recordings as chosen independently of the classifier’s confidence
  score. Clips picked because they have the highest scores contain fewer
  false positives than a random sample and would understate the
  false-positive rate, so draw the clips at random for this use.

## Citation

If you use crywolf, please cite the package (`citation("crywolf")`;
<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23385045>, which always resolves to the
latest version) and Miller et al. (2011), or Chambert et al. (2015) for
the observation-confirmation design.

Miller, D. A., Nichols, J. D., McClintock, B. T., Grant, E. H. C.,
Bailey, L. L., & Weir, L. A. (2011). Improving occupancy estimation when
two types of observational error occur: non-detection and species
misidentification. *Ecology*, 92, 1422–1428.
<https://doi.org/10.1890/10-1396.1>

Chambert, T., Miller, D. A. W., & Nichols, J. D. (2015). Modeling false
positive detections in species occurrence data under different study
designs. *Ecology*, 96, 332–339. <https://doi.org/10.1890/14-1507.1>

## Why “crywolf”?

The name comes from Aesop’s fable *The Boy Who Cried Wolf* (Perry Index
210), in which a shepherd boy raises the alarm about a wolf so many
times when there is none that nobody believes him when the wolf finally
comes
([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Boy_Who_Cried_Wolf)). An
automated detector is that boy: it sometimes cries “species!” when the
species is absent. Ignoring the false alarms biases occupancy estimates,
and discarding every alarm wastes the true ones. crywolf takes the
middle path: it uses a verified subset of detections to estimate how
often the detector cries wolf, and corrects for it.

The logo is a nod to the 1980s and to [“Cry
Wolf”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cry_Wolf_(A-ha_song)), the 1986
single by the Norwegian band a-ha from the album *Scoundrel Days*. It
borrows the synthwave look of the decade: a neon magenta frame on deep
purple, a striped setting sun, and a rounded display typeface. The wolf
howls in sound waves over a cyan audio equalizer, standing for the
acoustic recordings behind the package. The package has no connection
with the band, and the logo uses none of its artwork or lyrics.

## License

GPL (\>= 3). The wolf silhouette in the logo is *Canis lupus
monstrabilis* by Tracy A. Heath, from PhyloPic, in the public domain
(CC0 1.0).

# Package index

## Data

Assemble automated and verified detections and site covariates.

- [`fp_data()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_data.md) :
  Assemble data for a false-positive occupancy model
- [`fp_data_wide()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_data_wide.md)
  : Assemble data from detection matrices
- [`fp_to_unmarked()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_to_unmarked.md)
  : Convert data for unmarked::occuFP()

## Reading classifier output

Read BirdNET selection tables and reviewed clips, and build occasions.

- [`fp_read_birdnet()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_read_birdnet.md)
  : Read BirdNET selection tables
- [`fp_read_validation()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_read_validation.md)
  : Read the verdicts of a clip review
- [`fp_read_sheepdog()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_read_sheepdog.md)
  : Read an export of the sheepdog package
- [`fp_aggregate()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_aggregate.md)
  : Detections and confirmations per occasion
- [`fp_threshold_sweep()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_threshold_sweep.md)
  [`plot(`*`<fp_threshold_sweep>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_threshold_sweep.md)
  : Fit the model at several classifier thresholds

## Fitting

Fit the model and inspect, summarize, predict, and compare fits.

- [`fp_occu()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_occu.md) :
  Fit a Bayesian false-positive occupancy model
- [`fp_occu_mc()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_occu_mc.md)
  [`summary(`*`<fp_occu_mc>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_occu_mc.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.fp_occu_mc>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_occu_mc.md)
  [`print(`*`<fp_occu_mc>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_occu_mc.md)
  [`as_draws_df(`*`<fp_occu_mc>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_occu_mc.md)
  : Fit the model to draws of the detection histories
- [`fp_draws_data()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_draws_data.md)
  : Detection histories over the draws of a classifier calibration
- [`fp_priors()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_priors.md)
  : Prior settings for fp_occu()
- [`print(`*`<fp_occu>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_occu-methods.md)
  [`summary(`*`<fp_occu>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_occu-methods.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.fp_occu>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_occu-methods.md)
  [`coef(`*`<fp_occu>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_occu-methods.md)
  [`predict(`*`<fp_occu>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_occu-methods.md)
  [`loo(`*`<fp_occu>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_occu-methods.md)
  [`as_draws_df(`*`<fp_occu>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_occu-methods.md)
  : Methods for fp_occu fits
- [`crywolf-output`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/crywolf-output.md)
  [`output-names`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/crywolf-output.md)
  : Output names and interpretation
- [`fp_loo_weights()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_loo_weights.md)
  : Model weights by stacking
- [`fp_gap_prior()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_gap_prior.md)
  : A prior for the gap from validated detections
- [`fp_prior_predictive()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_prior_predictive.md)
  [`plot(`*`<fp_prior_predictive>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_prior_predictive.md)
  : Prior predictive check
- [`fp_ppc()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_ppc.md) :
  Posterior predictive check for a false-positive occupancy model
- [`fp_compile()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_compile.md)
  : Compile (or load) the Stan model
- [`fp_stan_file()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_stan_file.md)
  : Path to the Stan program

## Plots and site-level estimates

Coefficients, diagnostics, marginal effects, and occupancy of each site.

- [`plot(`*`<fp_occu>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/plot.fp_occu.md)
  : Plot a fitted model
- [`fp_effects()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_effects.md)
  [`plot(`*`<fp_effects>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_effects.md)
  : Marginal effect of a covariate
- [`fp_sites()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_sites.md)
  [`plot(`*`<fp_sites>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_sites.md)
  : Site-level estimates
- [`plot(`*`<fp_ppc>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/plot.fp_ppc.md)
  : Plot a posterior predictive check

## Simulation and calibration

Simulate false-positive regimes and check interval calibration for a
design.

- [`simulate_fp()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/simulate_fp.md)
  : Simulate data for a false-positive occupancy model
- [`fp_calibrate()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_calibrate.md)
  : Simulation-based calibration check for a study design
- [`fp_verification_curve()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_verification_curve.md)
  : Coverage as a function of verification effort
- [`fp_calibrate_fit()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_calibrate_fit.md)
  : Calibration of a fitted model on data like the real ones
- [`fp_sbc()`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_sbc.md)
  [`plot(`*`<fp_sbc>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/fp_sbc.md)
  : Simulation-based calibration
- [`simulate(`*`<fp_occu>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/simulate.fp_occu.md)
  : Simulate data from a fitted model
- [`plot(`*`<fp_calibration>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/plot.fp_calibration.md)
  : Plot the results of a calibration check

## Example data

Passive acoustic monitoring of the Common Pauraque in the Pantanal.

- [`curiango`](https://provetelab.org/crywolf/reference/curiango.md) :
  Passive acoustic monitoring of the Common Pauraque in the Pantanal
